_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, rendered at about 74px. The seven silhouettes are a ring with petals, a box with handles and a square post, a sphere on struts, a flat panel of parallel tubes, an open triangular truss, a wheeled rover, and a blunt gumdrop capsule. Class II avoids a robotic arm, because manipulators are an entry in class I, and uses a replaceable equipment box instead; class IV states explicitly that the panel is not a solar array, since a solar wing is already the space-launch sheet's class III. Nothing on this sheet duplicates that sheet's tiles: no launch vehicle, no globe, no dish, no flat terminal, no drum-shaped tug. The palette override has to forbid gold by name, because every real spacecraft surface is gold foil and the model reaches for it. Class VII ships as an edited image, not a generated one: every candidate drew the capsule with an open recessed top like a cup, and one generate-images.js edit pass closed it. Regenerating from this prompt alone will not reproduce the installed tile.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including multilayer insulation, foil blankets, solar cells and thermal coatings, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. No stars, no planets, no Earth, no space background, no exhaust and no thruster plumes; every subject sits alone on a plain flat light background. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Draw the subject as one whole object seen from outside. Do not draw a cutaway, a section view or an exploded assembly.

partPrompts.1: A single spacecraft docking ring seen three-quarter, standing tilted so its opening faces the viewer: a flat circular ring of moderate depth with a smooth outer rim, three identical flat petal-shaped guide vanes spaced evenly around the inner edge and angled outward, and a plain row of evenly spaced small bolt holes around the outer face. One ring alone, symmetrical and geometric. No spacecraft attached, no second ring, no hatch, no tunnel behind it, no cables.
partPrompts.2: A single replaceable equipment box sitting on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a plain rectangular case with a blank front face carrying two U-shaped handrails mounted side by side, one short square-section post standing up from the center of the top face with a squared knob on its end, and a plain mounting flange around the base. Blocky and simple, the two handrails and the single square post the identifying features. One box alone: no robot arm, no spacecraft, no wiring, no connectors, no markings.
partPrompts.3: A single spherical propellant tank seen three-quarter: one smooth sphere with a faint great-circle weld seam around its middle, carried a little above a flat surface by four straight splayed struts meeting a plain ring at its base, with one short pipe stub and a small square valve block at its top pole. The sphere dominates and the struts are thin. One tank alone: no plumbing runs, no second tank, no frame, no spacecraft, no frost.
partPrompts.4: A single spacecraft radiator panel seen three-quarter: a flat rectangular panel held at an angle on one short hinged arm rising from a plain square base, its face covered by many straight parallel tube runs spaced evenly across it from one long edge to the other, with a plain header pipe closing each end of that run. Flat and thin, the parallel tubes the identifying feature. Not a solar array: no grid of rectangular cells, no square divisions, no repeated panel segments, no second wing, no spacecraft body.
partPrompts.5: A single section of triangular lattice truss lying at an angle on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: three straight parallel tubular longerons at the corners of a triangle, joined along their length by short straight diagonal struts in a repeating zigzag, with a plain flat end fitting closing one end. Open and skeletal, so the background shows through the bracing, and clearly much longer than it is thick. One truss alone: no spacecraft, no panels, no robot arm, no joints being assembled.
partPrompts.6: A single planetary surface rover standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a low flat rectangular chassis carried on six plain wheels with visible cleats, three on each side on short rocker arms, with one short vertical mast standing at the front of the deck topped by a small plain box head, and a flat blank deck otherwise. Low, wide and clearly wheeled. One rover alone: no lander, no ramp, no regolith, no tracks in the dirt, no terrain, no antenna dish.
partPrompts.7: A single reentry capsule standing upright on a plain low stand, seen three-quarter: a blunt gumdrop shape, a truncated cone with gently curved sides rising to a small solid flat circular top deck that is completely closed over, sitting on a broad shallow domed base that reads clearly as a rounded heat shield, with a plain seam where the two meet and one small round hatch outline on the conical side. Squat, symmetrical, smooth and solid. The top must be a closed flat lid: not an open mouth, not a hollow rim, not a cup and not a funnel, and nothing on the capsule may read as an opening. One capsule alone: no parachutes, no lines, no scorch marks, no flames, no rocket, no ground detail.
